grade_rationale.text: Three authors are cited: Machal, Ralston and Afanasyev. The pages opened for Machal and for Ralston's Songs of the Russian People do not say they draw on Afanasyev, so they are counted as independent of him.
Ralston's Russian Folk-Tales takes its Leshy tale from Afanasyev's collection ('Afanasief, vii. No. 33'), so that book is counted with Afanasyev, not as a further source.
Machal records the silvan spirit Lésiy for the Russians.
Ralston records Lyeshy beliefs of the peasants of the Olonetsk and Archangel Governments, and separately a belief of Little-Russia.
Afanasyev records a Belarusian belief that the leshy's height depends on the trees he stands or walks by.
With at least two peoples (Russians and Belarusians, plus Little-Russia in Ralston) and three independent authors, the leshy is graded widely-attested.
